title: English Confession: faith differently affected by each part of the Word — chiefly receiving Christ
source_text: LXXIX. Atque hanc de illa quae sit per fidem applicatione, sententiam fuisse eorum qui Confessionem fidei in Anglia ante aliquot annos ediderunt, colligi posse videtur ex ea quam tradunt fidei salvificae descriptione, quam supra attulimus. Nam ex eorum sensu, Per hanc fidem Christianus verum credit quicquid est verbo Dei revelatum, propter Dei ipsius in verbo loquentis authoritatem, & differenter agit ac afficitur super singulis ejus quae continet istud verbum: mandatis scilicet, obsequens, ad minas contremiscens, & amplectens Dei promissiones, tam quae ad hanc vitam, quam quae ad futuram pertinent. Sed praecipui actus salutaris illius fidei sunt acceptare & recipere Christum, & in eo solo acquiescere ad justificationem, sanctificationem, & vitam aeternam.
pass_a_gloss: And that this was the opinion of those who published a Confession of faith in England some years ago concerning that application which is through faith seems able to be gathered from that description of saving faith which they hand down, which we brought forward above. For from their sense, Through this faith the Christian believes as true whatever is revealed by the word of God, because of the authority of God himself speaking in the word, and differently acts and is affected upon each of those things which that word contains: namely, obedient to the commands, trembling at the threatenings, and embracing God's promises, both those which pertain to this life and those which pertain to the future. But the chief acts of that saving faith are to accept and receive Christ, and to rest in him alone unto justification, sanctification, and eternal life.
pass_b_english: The mid-century English Confession seems to share that whole-Word application sense.

By this faith the Christian believes whatever God reveals, on God’s speaking authority, and is differently moved by each part: obeys commands, trembles at threats, embraces promises for this life and the next.
Chief saving acts: accept and receive Christ, and rest in him alone for justification, sanctification, and eternal life.
